questions.questionText: hour 15 minutes You must answer on the multiple choice answer sheet. You will need: Multiple choice answer sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) INSTRUCTIONS  There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions.  For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Write in soft pencil.  Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you.  Do not use correction fluid.  Do not write on any bar codes.  You may use a calculator. INFORMATION  The total mark for this paper is 30.  Each correct answer will score one mark.  Any rough working should be done on this question paper.

When choosing to buy two products, the satisfaction gained by the consumption of different combinations of these two products can be represented by an indifference curve. Which statement about such an indifference curve diagram is correct?

options.A: The range of indifference curves shows the combination of products a consumer can purchase with a given income.
options.B: If an indifference curve is a downward-sloping straight line, the principle of diminishing marginal utility must be operating.
options.C: Indifference curves never cross, because this means that a consumer would be indifferent between combinations of two goods, even when one combination provides more of each good.
options.D: The gap between indifference curves is always constant.

questions.questionText: Negative externalities, such as air pollution due to car emissions, can cause damage to people’s health in cities. Which response is most likely to occur from this situation?

options.A: car manufacturers will automatically bear any external costs
options.B: market failure will be resolved when private costs equal external costs
options.C: most people will decide to use buses rather than cars
options.D: some form of government intervention to improve economic efficiency

questions.questionText: The merger of two large firms in the Singapore market supplying taxis and private hire vehicles resulted in a single firm with 80% of the market. The remaining 20% of the market consisted of thousands of independent taxi drivers. Which statement best describes what has effectively occurred in the market structure?

options.A: The market has become monopolistically competitive.
options.B: The market has changed from an oligopoly to a monopoly.
options.C: The market has changed from perfect competition to an oligopoly.
options.D: The market remains an oligopoly.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the cost and revenue curves of a profit-maximising, monopolistically competitive firm in long-run equilibrium. costs, AC revenue MC P AR MR O Q output Which statement correctly describes the performance of this firm?

options.A: It is allocatively efficient.
options.B: It is making abnormal losses.
options.D: It is making normal profits.

questions.questionText: A firm changes its aim and chooses to produce where marginal revenue (MR) is zero instead of where MR is equal to marginal cost (MC). Which explanation for this is not correct?

options.A: The firm wishes to increase sales.
options.B: The firm wishes to increase its output.
options.C: The firm wishes to reduce prices.
options.D: The firm wishes to gain more profits.

questions.questionText: A firm operating in the airline industry uses third degree price discrimination. Which condition is most likely to allow this to happen?

options.A: Consumers are able to buy cheaply and then sell the product at a higher price.
options.B: Price elasticity of demand is the same for all consumers in the market.
options.C: The firm faces a perfectly elastic demand curve.
options.D: The firm is able to keep the different market segments separate.

questions.questionText: What is not an example of a moral hazard?

options.A: People with a higher risk of unemployment are more likely to undertake training.
options.B: People with free dental care are less likely to take care of their teeth with good oral hygiene.
options.C: People with insurance against car theft are more likely to park their car in high crime areas.
options.D: People with unemployment benefits are less likely to undertake retraining if they become unemployed.

questions.questionText: In recent years, the fuel cost of operating a jet aircraft has declined. Over the same period, improved design has led to much quieter aircraft. How would this affect the marginal private cost (MPC) and the marginal external cost (MEC) of air travel?

options.A: a downward shift of both the MPC and the MEC curves
options.B: a downward shift of the MPC curve and a movement left along the MEC curve
options.C: a movement left along both the MPC and the MEC curves
options.D: a movement left along the MPC curve and a downward shift of the MEC curve

questions.questionText: Firm K operates in a competitive market. Firm L is a monopsony employer. Both firms are operating at an equilibrium level of output. Trade unions are introduced with the result that wages in each firm are increased. What is the likely effect on each firm if trade unions enter the labour market? firm K firm L

options.A: employment will decrease employment will decrease
options.B: employment will decrease employment will increase
options.C: employment will increase employment will decrease
options.D: employment will increase employment will increase

questions.questionText: A backward-sloping supply curve of labour is one where, beyond a certain point, the supply of labour

options.A: decreases as the demand for labour rises.
options.B: increases as the demand for labour rises.
options.D: increases as wages rise.

questions.questionText: What is the economic result of a universal basic income (UBI)? reduces the improves incentive to work equality

options.A: no no
options.B: no yes
options.D: yes yes

questions.questionText: Which combination of fiscal policy measures would be most effective in reducing income inequality? top rates of value of state indirect taxes income tax benefits

options.A: increase increase increase
options.B: increase reduce increase
options.D: reduce reduce reduce

questions.questionText: At present, motorists who drive their cars within area 1 on the map pay a daily congestion charge of $8. X YY Z area 1 aaarrreeeaaa 222 Which car journeys would decrease in number if the congestion charge area were extended to include area 2?

options.A: journeys from point X to point Z
options.B: journeys from point X to point Y
options.C: journeys from point Y to point Z
options.D: journeys from point Z to point Y

questions.questionText: What is most likely to lead to an increase in the size of the national income?

options.A: a fall in interest rates on savings accounts
options.B: a fall in the prices of imported goods
options.D: an increase in direct taxes

questions.questionText: Which government policy is most likely to improve occupational mobility?

options.A: decreased income tax rates
options.B: increased government spending on education and training
options.D: increased subsidies to firms to employ school leavers

questions.questionText: The table shows the marginal propensity to consume (MPC), marginal propensity to save (MPS), marginal rate of taxation (MRT) and marginal propensity to import (MPM) for a four-sector economy. value MPC 0.5 MPS 0.2 MRT 0.2 MPM 0.1 What is the size of the multiplier?
What is likely to happen when the productive capacity of a free enterprise economy increases over a long period of time?

options.A: Future generations will be less well-off than present generations.
options.B: Increasing the production of one good cannot be done without decreasing the production of another.
options.C: Individuals will have more choices due to a wider range of consumer goods.
options.D: Rising levels of output will cause per capita incomes to equalise.

questions.questionText: The accelerator principle refers to a relationship between investment and

options.A: the level of GDP.
options.B: changes in GDP.
options.D: changes in interest rates.

questions.questionText: What is likely to be the effect of an increase in the budget deficit?

options.A: an increase in effective demand
options.B: an increase in unemployment
options.D: a reduction in the volume of spending

questions.questionText: The table gives details of the inflation and unemployment rates for different countries in 2008 and 2011. inflation rate unemployment rate (% per annum) (% of workforce) country 2008 2011 2008 2011 Canada 2.38 2.89 6.15 7.47 France 3.16 2.29 7.81 9.68 Germany 2.75 2.48 7.60 5.98 Japan 1.37 –0.28 3.99 4.55 Which countries experienced a trade-off between their inflation and unemployment rates?

options.A: Canada and Germany
options.B: Canada only
options.D: France only

questions.questionText: Which government policy would boost economic growth but not necessarily promote economic development?

options.A: creating a more equal distribution of income and wealth
options.B: diverting government spending from industry to education
options.C: encouraging the extraction of finite natural resources
options.D: introducing tighter controls on air pollution

questions.questionText: Which policy measure to encourage economic growth might be based on the concept of the Laffer curve?

options.A: cuts in direct taxes
options.B: exchange rate depreciation
options.D: quantitative easing

questions.questionText: The exchange rate of an economy appreciates. Assuming that the Marshall–Lerner condition holds in this economy, what is the likely outcome for imported inflation and unemployment? imported inflation unemployment

options.A: falls falls
options.B: falls rises
options.D: rises rises

questions.questionText: Which characteristics are most commonly found in low-income countries? capital-output saving ratio ratio

options.A: low low
options.B: high low
options.D: high high

questions.questionText: What has not accompanied global economic growth over the last 25 years?

options.A: a depletion of non-renewable resources
options.B: decreased international trade
options.D: increased atmospheric pollution

questions.questionText: When assessing income distribution in an economy, which change in the Gini coefficient suggests that a country is distributing its income more equally?

options.A: It has moved closer to one.
options.B: It has moved closer to zero.
options.C: It has moved from negative to positive.
options.D: It has moved from positive to negative.

questions.questionText: In 2021, a very large cargo ship carrying over 18000 cargo containers blocked the Suez Canal for seven days. It delayed over 350 other cargo ships, causing shortages of products in markets around the world as supplies were disrupted. Which consequence of globalisation is best illustrated by this event?

options.A: cheaper products for consumers
options.B: greater choice of products for consumers
options.D: increased migration of labour between countries

questions.questionText: The table shows data for Namibia and Spain from 2014 to 2017. Namibia Spain 2014 2017 2014 2017 real GDP per capita ($) 6113 6013 29399 32283 health spending per capita ($) 452 447 2671 2506 (assuming constant price levels) What can be concluded about whether there has been an increase in economic growth and economic development in Namibia and Spain between 2014 and 2017? economic economic growth development

options.A: Namibia only Namibia only
options.B: Spain only Namibia and Spain
options.D: neither country Spain only
